About CFL

A small nonprofit with a simple job: keep good housing affordable.

CFL HOUSING CORP is a Florida nonprofit corporation based in Melbourne, Florida. We were formed in 2007 and are recognized by the IRS as a 501(c)(3) public charity. Our work is acquiring existing apartment communities, fixing what needs fixing, and operating them as affordable housing — patiently, honestly, and for the long term.

“BEST honorable in all things.”— The principle CFL was built on, passed down in our president's family and applied to every deal, every resident, and every partner.

Why preservation matters

When an affordable community is sold and rents jump, families don't just pay more — they move, change schools, and lose their footing. Buying existing housing and keeping it affordable is faster and cheaper than building new, and it protects the people already living there.

We look hardest at communities that are working but tired — properties that need a steady owner, modest rehab, and rents kept within reach.

How we're different as a buyer

  • Nonprofit structureAs a 501(c)(3), we can use tools for-profit buyers can't — including bargain sales, charitable gifts of equity, tax-exempt financing, and housing tax credits — to make a fair deal work.
  • Real numbers firstWe underwrite on trailing actuals — real income, real expenses, a real rent roll. No offer on a guess.
  • Long-term ownerWe buy to hold and operate, with affordability kept in place for 15–30 years where a program requires it.
What we do

Acquire. Rehab. Operate. Keep it affordable.

Four parts, done in order, on every property.

Step 1

Acquire & preserve

We buy 100+ unit multifamily communities, including distressed properties and hotel conversions that can become permanent housing.

Step 2

Rehab & stabilize

We address deferred maintenance, safety, and capital needs first — then stabilize occupancy with fair rents and respectful management.

Step 3

Finance responsibly

We stack the right tools for each deal: assumable loans, tax-exempt bonds, 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, HOME, SAIL, and lender partnerships — including CRA-motivated banks.

Step 4

Operate for residents

Day-to-day operations run with respect for residents — clear communication, prompt repairs, and costs checked item by item against cash flow.

Existing communities

Up-and-running apartment properties where affordability is at risk of being lost. This is our first priority.

Veterans housing

Housing for veterans, including hotel-to-housing conversions paired with service partners and HUD-VASH where available.

Seniors & families

Communities suited to older adults and families — including one-bedroom homes, which are in short supply and high demand.

Who we serve

Housing for the people who keep a community running.

We welcome affordability programs — Section 8, LIHTC restrictions, and extended-use agreements are a plus for us, not a problem.

Working families

Entry-level and workforce rents that leave room for everything else a family has to pay for.

Seniors

Stable, well-maintained homes for older adults on fixed incomes, including HUD Section 202-type housing.

Veterans

Permanent housing for veterans, with service partners where support is needed.

Students & military

Student housing near colleges and off-base rentals for active-duty families near bases.

People with disabilities

Accessible set-asides, including Section 811-type housing, with a service partner where needed.

People rebuilding

Housing for people exiting homelessness, in reentry, or fleeing abuse — always with a qualified service partner.

Residents already there

When we buy a community, the people living there come first. Preservation means they can stay.

Communities

Cities and counties get a stable, tax-conscious, long-term owner who keeps housing in the local stock.

For owners, brokers & partners

We are looking to buy. Real offer requires real numbers.

If you own or represent a multifamily property, we want to hear from you. Send the numbers and we will do the math ourselves — plainly and promptly. We are humble, patient, and serious, and we will tell you straight if a price can work.

Property size
100 units or more (beds count for student housing)
Location
Nationwide mainland U.S. — priority Florida, Southeast & Texas
Property types
Operating communities, distressed / REO, lease-ups, and hotel conversions
Our screen
8% yield and about $3,000 per unit per year in net cash flow, on trailing actuals — deals below it are looked at case by case
What to send
Units & price, trailing 12-month income & expenses, current rent roll, occupancy, loan balance / rate / assumability, tax & insurance bills. A phone photo of a document counts.
Loan holders
Please include servicer / lender contact if a loan may be assumed — we pursue assumption and new financing in parallel.
For sellers

“I'll buy your property if you give me the down payment — legally.”

That's a bargain sale. Part of the price is paid in cash and financing, and part is a charitable gift of equity to a 501(c)(3). For the right seller, the tax benefit of the gift can help close a gap no ordinary buyer can close. We explain it in writing, with your CPA in the loop, before anything is signed.

For developers & lenders

Bring us a tired property. We'll bring the structure.

For rehab projects, CFL can bring 4% credits and tax-exempt bonds (or 9% credits for substantial rehab), exemption work, and cheaper financing — the developer takes the fee, CFL owns and operates. Lenders: affordable loans can count toward CRA community-development goals.

Common questions

Straight answers.

Are you a real 501(c)(3)? Can I verify it?

Yes. CFL HOUSING CORP, EIN 11-3822012, is a Florida nonprofit recognized as a 501(c)(3) public charity (IRS Letter 947, Jan. 6, 2023, effective May 15, 2022). You can look us up in IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search and in Florida Sunbiz (N07000008398).

Do you have apartments available to rent right now?

Not yet listed here. CFL is currently acquiring its first communities. If you are looking for housing help today, contact your local housing authority or call 211. When we have homes available, vacancies and how to apply will be posted on this page.

I own a property. What happens after I contact you?

Send what you have — trailing income and expenses, a rent roll, and the loan details. We grade it on our screen (8% yield, ~$3,000/unit/year cash flow on actuals), and we reply with a plain opinion. No offer and no price talk until the real numbers are in hand — that protects you and us.

Do grants and tax credits pay for a whole purchase?

No — and anyone who tells you otherwise isn't being straight. Grants, HOME, CDBG, FHLBank awards, SAIL, bonds, and tax credits fill gaps and lower financing costs. They run on annual, competitive rounds through a city, county, state, or member bank, and they carry 15–30 year affordability commitments, which we accept. The purchase itself is funded by debt, cash, and — where it fits — a bargain-sale gift.

How can I support CFL?

The most useful help right now is a property lead, a lender introduction, or a partnership on a rehab. Financial gifts to a 501(c)(3) may be tax-deductible to the extent allowed by law — talk to your tax advisor, and contact us first so we can provide a proper receipt.
